title: Requirements specification for vertical production press hydraulic ram
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Open-circuit fixed-displacement pump topology with the tank supplying pump suction, pump pressure branching directly to the relief valve and the open-centre 4/3 DCV, and all relief/DCV returns going directly to the tank. The DCV drives a single double-acting press cylinder through a dual pilot-operated check load lock at the actuator ports. Downward motion is represented as cylinder extension. The cap-side branch is direct through the load lock. The rod-side branch passes through the load lock to a shared rod-exhaust node represented by repeated connections from LoadLock.B1; one leg is the pressure-compensated one-way flow control and the other is the position-operated bypass. The bypass is open for rapid approach and return/hold venting, and closed during working feed and final press so rod-side exhaust must pass through the pressure-compensated meter-out path. The open-centre DCV neutral unloads the fixed pump and vents both work-line/pilot-release sides to tank so the pilot-operated check can reseat for the upper-position hold.

motion_control_decisions.justification: This is the intentionally faster downward phase before slower feed/pressing phases; stated load is negligible and net moving weight is included in the specified loads.

The same downward motion direction changes from fast approach to a slower feed speed; no load-independent or adjustable speed requirement is stated, so non-compensated throttled control is inferred for the slow phase. Load is stated as resistive.
This phase remains in the slower downward speed range after rapid approach, with increased force demand; no load-independent or adjustable speed requirement is stated. Load is stated as resistive.
Only a return time and resistance are specified; no deliberate throttling, adjustment, load-independent control, or overrunning behavior is required for this powered resistive return phase.
Static holding is explicitly required while the power unit is unloaded; dynamic metering is not relevant, and a load-retention strategy is required to prevent creep/descent.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank provides the suction and return boundary; Pump supplies the circuit; the open-centre DCV neutral unloads fixed pump flow to Tank.R during the upper hold.
ReliefValve.P is connected directly to Pump.P and ReliefValve.T returns directly to Tank.R, providing the topology for the 100 bar maximum system pressure limit subject to final setting and sizing.

The 4/3 open-centre DCV commands extend, retract, and neutral states for the double-acting press cylinder. The dual pilot-operated check is installed at both actuator ports for the upper-position hold. The rod-side exhaust path includes one pressure-compensated flow control for working feed and final press, with a position-operated bypass in parallel for fast approach and unmetered return/venting.

For slow downward feed and final press, RapidFeedBypass is closed and rod-side exhaust flows from PressCylinder.Rod through LoadLock.B2/B1 and RodMeterOutFlowControl.A-to-B to DCV.B. For rapid approach, RapidFeedBypass is open around the same metering path.

The dual pilot-operated check locally blocks reverse actuator-port flow during hold. DCV neutral vents A and B to Tank.R, allowing the valve-side/pilot-release pressures at LoadLock.A1 and LoadLock.B1 to decay so the checks can reseat.
Final pressing force is produced by the cylinder area under the pressure limit established by the relief valve; no separate force-stage valve is required by the selected topology.

design_decisions.decision: Use a fixed-displacement pump with an open-centre 4/3 DCV neutral for unloading.
design_decisions.rationale: This is the minimal simple supply architecture; the open-centre DCV neutral provides pump unloading and vents A/B work lines while the load lock, not the spool, holds the ram.
driven_by: upper hold with unloaded power unit

design_decisions.decision: Connect the main relief valve directly from pump pressure to tank return.
design_decisions.rationale: A relief valve on the pump pressure branch is the selected catalog mechanism for overpressure protection and the 100 bar maximum system pressure requirement; the actual setting is deferred to sizing/specification.
driven_by: maximum system pressure not exceeding 100 bar

design_decisions.decision: Use one dual pilot-operated check at the actuator ports for upper-position holding.
design_decisions.rationale: The timed upper hold should not rely on DCV spool leakage. A dual load lock avoids depending on confirmation of the load-supporting chamber while still allowing commanded release by opposite-line pressure.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one pressure-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-side exhaust meter-out path.
design_decisions.rationale: The feed and final press phases share the same load-independent throttled meter-out requirement at the rod chamber exhaust, so one pressure-compensated flow control is used in the controlled A-to-B exhaust direction.

design_decisions.decision: Use a position-operated bypass in parallel with the single rod-side meter-out path.
design_decisions.rationale: The bypass is open for rapid approach and closes after the position trip so slow feed/final press exhaust cannot bypass the flow control. Reopening it during return/hold provides an unmetered return and vent path without adding electrical sensing.
driven_by: no simultaneous unmetered bypass during metered phases

design_decisions.decision: Do not add a separate force-stage valve for final pressing.
design_decisions.rationale: The final press has the same selected downward speed-control topology as working feed; increased force is a sizing outcome of cylinder area and pressure under the relief limit.

assumptions: Downward ram travel is represented as cylinder extension and upward return as cylinder retraction.

The selected dual pilot-operated check uses its listed valve-side ports A1 and B1 as the internal cross-pilot pressure sources; no separate external pilot ports are available in the selected generic metadata.

During upper hold, the position-operated bypass may be open/reset while the load lock holds the actuator; this supports rod-side valve-line venting and does not create actuator motion because the DCV is neutral and the load lock is unpiloted.
Relief setting, pump displacement, cylinder dimensions, pressure ratings, and leakage ratings are deferred to sizing/specification.

research_coverage.summary: The evidence is strong for relief/stall pressure limiting, 4/3 directional control of a double-acting cylinder, meter-out pressure-compensated feed control on the rod-side exhaust, and pilot-operated-check/load-control holding principles. However, critical gaps remain: the open-circuit power-unit evidence does not actually cite the pump suction/reservoir inlet leg, and the required automatic multi-speed/force phase-transition topology is not yet supported beyond generic meter-out speed control. Because those gaps affect mandatory topology and automatic sequence behavior, design should not proceed yet.

items.rationale: Relief-valve placement, fixed-displacement pump unloading, pressure-to-tank relief return, open-center/unloading behavior, and stall/deadhead protection are well supported by T1 with textbook/technical citations. But the finding itself states that the pump suction line from tank/reservoir was not explicitly verified by a citation. Since this need explicitly requires complete suction, pump, relief, return, and reservoir topology, the suction/reservoir-to-pump inlet connection remains an unsupported critical claim.

T2 supports using a 3-position, 4-way directional control valve for a double-acting cylinder, with cited evidence for extend, retract, and neutral/hold states. It also provides supported neutral-center considerations for pump unloading and pilot-operated-check compatibility, including A/B-to-tank neutral behavior for pilot pressure decay.

T3 supports the load-independent throttled meter-out portions of the profile using a pressure-compensated flow control with reverse-flow check in the rod-side exhaust path, and T2 supports retract/neutral states. What is missing is cited topology for the complete ordered multi-speed sequence: unrestricted rapid approach, automatic transition to controlled work feed, automatic transition to final press/pressure-force phase, and return/hold sequencing. Current evidence explicitly says it does not provide a complete press-specific circuit or two-speed force-switching schematic.

T2 and T5 support the essential load-holding pattern: do not rely on a leaking metal-to-metal spool for a vertical loaded cylinder; use pilot-operated check valves or equivalent load-locking; place the valve at/near the cylinder work port; pilot it from the opposite work port; and use a neutral condition that vents A/B so pilot pressure drops and checks close. T3 also supports controlled meter-out motion for overrunning/vertical load control, with a pressure-intensification caution.

The topology-level requirement for leak-resistant holding with the power unit unloaded is supported by T2/T5/followup: pilot-operated check valves are cited as preventing drift/positively locking pressurized loads, supporting vertical-cylinder static load holding, and preventing cylinder creep; they should be installed near the cylinder port and released only by pilot pressure from the opposite work port. T2 supplies the important neutral compatibility evidence that A/B-to-tank lets pilot pressure drop and blocked A/B can keep checks open. The exact 10-minute performance will still depend on component leakage ratings, cylinder internal leakage, and sealing practice, but exact catalog selection is not a topology research need.

The slow/feed speed-control element is supported by T3, and relief-limited maximum pressure is supported by T1. But the critical automatic fast/slow and low/high-force or pressure switching topology is not yet supported. Missing claims include how rapid approach bypasses or avoids the metered rod-exhaust restriction, what component automatically switches the circuit into the throttled feed path, and what component/connection automatically changes between the 12 kN and 50 kN force/pressure phases.

T1 provides direct cited evidence that fixed-volume pump circuits require relief protection, that a relief valve opens at its set pressure and returns oil to reservoir, and that it is essential during actuator stall/end-of-stroke/deadheading. Connection guidance supports placing the relief valve in parallel from the pressure line to tank and setting it to the 100 bar maximum system pressure.

missing_or_weak_information: Critical unsupported claim: reservoir/tank must feed the pump inlet through a suction line as part of the complete open-circuit power-unit topology; current evidence only verifies relief/unloading/return-to-tank behavior.

Critical unsupported claim: automatic transition from unrestricted rapid approach to meter-out controlled feed/final press, including the valve or control element that opens/closes a bypass around the flow control or otherwise changes flow path at the transition point.

Critical unsupported claim: automatic low-force/high-force or low-pressure/high-pressure switching between the 12 kN work-feed and 50 kN final-press phases, including essential connection/placement of sequence, pressure, unloading, or electrohydraulic control valves.

Noncritical limitation: load holding for a full 10 minutes still requires later component leakage-rating and cylinder-seal verification; topology evidence supports pilot-operated check/load-locking but not exact leakage performance.

design_review.summary: The proposed topology functionally satisfies the brief: open-circuit pump/tank/relief supply is direct, the open-centre DCV provides extend/retract/neutral with pump unloading and work-line venting, the dual pilot-check load lock is placed at the actuator ports with opposite-line release, and the rod-side exhaust uses a single pressure-compensated meter-out path with a position-operated bypass open only for rapid/return and closed during feed/final press. No functional topology errors were identified.

validation.summary: Deterministic validation: valid. Engineering review: valid. The proposed topology functionally satisfies the brief: open-circuit pump/tank/relief supply is direct, the open-centre DCV provides extend/retract/neutral with pump unloading and work-line venting, the dual pilot-check load lock is placed at the actuator ports with opposite-line release, and the rod-side exhaust uses a single pressure-compensated meter-out path with a position-operated bypass open only for rapid/return and closed during feed/final press. No functional topology errors were identified.

policy.approach: Smallest proved standard design: final-press force governs the cylinder, a conventional force-proportion rod is used, and the pump is aimed just inside the return-speed lower bound.

actuator_decisions.justification: The final pressing phase has the governing load. The tool chain gives required piston area 6172.8 mm2 at this design pressure and, after ISO selection, a 100 mm bore with 7854.0 mm2 cap area. The force-proportion rod selection is 56 mm, giving 5391.0 mm2 annulus area and cap:annulus ratio 1.457.

supply_decision.justification: With the 56 mm rod, the return requirement governs pump sizing. The tool flow at the aimed return speed is 42.858 L/min, so the standard pump is 32.0 cm3/rev delivering 43.2 L/min. At the pressure ceiling this selects 8.471 kW shaft power and an 11.0 kW motor.

setting_decisions.basis: The verified worst final-press pump pressure is 70.85910220161148 bar and the verified worst return pump pressure is 8.995131637947516 bar, so a 100 bar relief clears the working envelope while matching the stated system ceiling.
Flow setting, not pressure setting: set for the tool metered rod-exhaust flow of 10.782 L/min for the 2 m/min feed and press speed; nominal valve size NG4 rated 20.0 L/min.

engineering_notes: Evaluation verdict: PROVED, with 8 PROVED, 0 UNDECIDED, 0 REFUTED.
Verified velocities are 5.500394833255903 m/min fast approach, 2.11999999999788 m/min work feed, 2.11999999999788 m/min final press, and 8.013395736095429 m/min return.
DCV and main flow path size from full pump delivery: NG6 rated 60.0 L/min for 43.2 L/min pump flow.
The pressure-compensated meter-out valve is sized on rod exhaust, not full pump flow: NG4 rated 20.0 L/min for 10.782 L/min.
The dual pilot-operated check must be specified with leakage performance adequate for the upper hold interval.
open_issues: Verifier thermal finding: 3.14 kW crosses the relief in the worst phase, while the assumed 160 L reservoir sheds roughly 1.60 kW; heat rejection must be addressed in detailed specification.
Confirm actual cylinder mounting/port assignment and leakage acceptance criterion for the ten-minute upper hold.
